subject: Post-call: FinSight observability & evals — recap and proposed next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finsight.ai>, Aisha Bhattacharya <aishab@finsight.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: FinSight observability & evals — recap and proposed next steps

Hi Sanjay / Aisha —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our 30-minute discovery so we all have the same picture and clear next steps. I tried to keep this tight — let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points you shared
- Production drift: model responses have slowly degraded on edge cases over the last 4–6 weeks and you lack a reliable regression alerting process.
- Visibility gaps: current telemetry covers API errors and latency but not token-level latency, per-route cost, or golden-prompt regression traces.
- Slow eval cycles: creating and running prompt evals against new model variants takes 2–3 weeks and manual orchestration.

Current stack
- Serving: internal endpoints on k8s backed by mixed GPU fleet (A100 + T4 standby).
- Telemetry: Prometheus + Grafana for infra; light-weight app logs to ELK.
- Evals: ad hoc Jupyter notebooks + GitHub actions for scheduled runs.

Success criteria you mentioned
1) <0.5% regression rate on priority customer prompt set (Golden Set) with automated detection and alerting.
2) Per-route token cost visibility at the function/feature level.
3) 24–48 hour turnaround for an eval + rollout decision when testing a new model/quantization profile.
4) Tracing hooks into KV cache and prefix matches for high-volume routes.

What Redwood can deliver (high level)
- Eval pipeline: scheduled & on-demand evals, golden prompt sets, automated regression detection, and report artifacts.
- Observability: per-route dashboards (latency, cost, token breakdown), tracing hooks (KV cache hits, prefix matches), and per-request sampling for replay.
- Rollout controls: canary percentages, automatic rollback on regression, and pre-flight eval gates.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
- Marcus to provision a short instrumented demo (sample traffic) and share a Live Grafana dashboard: target by Tue 19 Jan.
- FinSight to share: golden prompt set (CSV), 3 representative routes, and one recent failing example (can be redacted): target by Mon 18 Jan.
- Redwood to provide an Eval Readiness checklist + a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) we can iterate on: I attached the checklist and MAP workbook.

Owners & timeline
- Kimberly (Redwood): commercial + MAP, follow up on pricing and contract cadence.
- Marcus (Redwood, SE): demo instrumentation + dashboards.
- Laura (Redwood, AE/solutions): technical scoping for tracing hooks and rollout policy.
- Sanjay / Aisha (FinSight): deliver golden set, routes, and infra contact for access.

If that aligns, I’ll send a short calendar invite for an instrumentation demo next Tuesday and upload the MAP to the shared Drive.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-eval-readiness-checklist.pdf, finsight-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinSight observability & evals — recap and proposed next steps

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear summary. All aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications:
- Golden set: we have ~120 prompts but will surface a prioritized subset (~20) for the initial eval — will send CSV by Monday.
- Routes: tracker-generation, invoice-extraction, and customer-summary are the three we want to instrument first.
- Access: our DevOps team uses a bastion for admin access; I’ll loop them in on the demo invite so Marcus can request a short-lived role.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood’s regression alerts be routed to PagerDuty or should we use a webhook to our ELK for the first pass?
2) For the eval run time estimate — do you have a ballpark token-cost/time estimate for the 20-prompt golden set across 3 candidate models?

Thanks —
Sanjay Rao
Head of Product, FinSight Analytics
Sanjay.Rao@finsight.ai | +1 (650) 555-0122

Subject: Re: Post-call: FinSight observability & evals — recap and proposed next steps

Hi Sanjay / Aisha —

Short answers to your questions and a bit of technical framing so we can size the integration work: 

1) Alerting integrations: Redwood supports direct PagerDuty routing (recommended) and also webhooks if you prefer to ingest into ELK. We can wire both during the POC; PagerDuty is lower-lift for on-call routing.

2) Eval cost/time estimate: for a 20-prompt canonical set (average 350 tokens per prompt + response) across 3 candidate models (LLaMA-3-70b, Mistral-XX, and a quantized 13B internal variant) — expect ~30–90 minutes wall time to run in parallel on a dedicated small pool, and token cost in the order of a few hundred thousand tokens (we’ll provide a precise estimate once we know max sequence length / sampling params).

Technical notes:
- Tracing hooks: we’ll need a small instrumentation library (2–3 endpoints) that annotates requests with route id and golden-prompt id; Marcus will demo a sample.
- Rollout guardrails: our default is a 5% canary + automatic rollback if any golden-prompt shows >0.5% regression in accuracy/score, but we can customize thresholds.

I’ll prep a short tech brief for the demo. Marcus — I’ll sync with you offline about the sample traffic generator and required ports.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: I uploaded the Eval Readiness checklist and a draft MAP workbook to Drive and linked them above. Please comment on the MAP before Wednesday so we can finalize commercial terms.

If there are no objections I’ll send the calendar invite and include a brief pre-read.

Thanks all —
Kimberly
